replaces: v1 YOLO26n pipeline (models/best.pt, models/best_full_integer_quant_vela.tflite) — DEPRECATED, root-caused as unsupported by SenseCraft/GV2 firmware, kept for reference only
architecture: YOLOv8n (Ultralytics 8.3.203, classic TensorFlow SavedModel -> TFLiteConverter export path, NOT the newer litert_torch backend)
why_this_architecture: Seeed's own official Grove Vision AI V2 deployment docs (wiki.seeedstudio.com/ma_deploy_yolov8) document YOLOv8n as a supported architecture for GV2/SenseCraft. YOLO26 was confirmed unsupported by Seeed staff on their own forum (SenseCraft does not currently parse YOLO26 metadata), which is the root cause of the v1 model's boxes:[] failure on real hardware.

input.note: 192x192, NOT 224x224 -- this is the resolution Seeed's official YOLOv8 pipeline docs specify for GV2, and is intentionally different from the v1 YOLO26 model's 224x224.

output.layout: channels = [box_x, box_y, box_w, box_h, cls0_red, cls1_yellow, cls2_green, cls3_sample], 756 = sum of anchor grid cells at strides 8/16/32 for imgsz=192 (24x24 + 12x12 + 6x6)
output.note: This is the raw one2many-style anchor output required for Ethos-U55 deployment (no on-chip NMS/TopK). SenseCraft/SSCMA firmware performs the class-argmax + NMS decode on-device -- this is the same output contract Seeed's official YOLOv8 GV2 models use.

training.dataset_source: Rebuilt from annotations.json files inside the user's Seperate_Images.zip (SenseCraft per-class training exports) -- real pixel-space bounding boxes, not synthetic labels
training.KNOWN_LIMITATION: Training images are single-object, plain-background photos captured via SenseCraft's own capture workflow -- NOT the cluttered, multi-object competition scene. High val metrics reflect performance on data resembling the training distribution, not a guarantee of real-arena generalization. This caveat applies equally to the v1 model and is not new to this pipeline.

export_toolchain.ultralytics_version: 8.3.203 (deliberately pinned -- ultralytics >=8.4.83 defaults to a newer litert_torch export backend that produces NCHW float32-wrapped I/O incompatible with clean Vela compilation; this was reproduced and confirmed during this session, see docs/YOLOV8N_PIPELINE.md)
export_toolchain.export_command: yolo export model=best.pt format=tflite imgsz=192 int8 data=yolo_dataset/data.yaml

vela_compile_result.note: Clean single-op compile, no CPU-fallback DEQUANTIZE/QUANTIZE wrapper ops -- this is the same clean-compile signature as the originally-provided v1 file, now achieved starting from a supported architecture.

offline_validation.confidence_test: PASS -- 60/60 held-out val images (15 per class) produced the correct top class from BOTH PyTorch (mean conf 0.965) and the pre-Vela INT8 TFLite (mean conf 0.725, narrower dynamic range from int8 quantization of the class-score tensor -- expected and not a defect). 0/60 images produced zero detections, unlike the v1 model's persistent boxes:[] on real hardware.
offline_validation.NOT_TESTED: Actual Ethos-U55 NPU execution via Vela's command stream -- this requires real GV2 hardware or Arm's Ethos-U simulator, neither available in this environment. The confidence test above validates the INT8 math Vela compiles 1:1 (Vela only schedules ops for the NPU, it does not change arithmetic), but the on-device SenseCraft/SSCMA postprocessing (anchor decode + NMS + metadata parsing) has NOT been exercised.
